stem: Meera chews a piece of plain chapati for two minutes at home and notices that it begins to taste sweet. She then tests the chewed chapati with iodine solution. Which observation would best support the conclusion that her saliva has changed starch into sugar?

options.text: The chewed chapati turns blue-black with iodine, showing starch is still present.
The chewed chapati shows little or no blue-black colour with iodine, showing some starch has been changed into sugar.
The chewed chapati feels softer, showing that saliva has made it wet.
The chewed chapati tastes sweet only because chapati is naturally sweet.

teacher.key_rationale: The decision requires inferring starch-to-sugar breakdown from a weakened iodine reaction: loss of the blue-black colour after chewing indicates saliva's amylase acted on starch. Option B is the only observation consistent with that inference; A contradicts it, C is irrelevant wetting, D denies the saliva mechanism.
